compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Establish the `dso_ci_review/` Python package skeleton that can run a single specialist call against Anthropic via LiteLLM, verify the LiteLLM transport, and capture pre-migration golden corpus + duration baseline from the existing bash runner. This is the walking skeleton — it proves the migration path end-to-end before we replace the orchestration.

**Why**: Subsequent stories (S2 provider abstraction, S3 full orchestration, S4 parity test, S5 unit tests) all depend on a transport-decision artifact and a deterministic baseline. Capturing both before any bash code is touched ensures the pre-migration measurements remain available throughout the epic.

**Scope**:
- IN: Minimal `dso_ci_review/` package skeleton; LiteLLM transport verification gate (per Anthropic + OpenAI provider paths); pre-migration golden corpus capture (input fixture diffs + LLM provider request/response pairs recorded via VCR/cassettes or saved raw JSON for reproducibility); pre-migration p50/p95 CI review-job duration capture on fixture corpus.
- OUT: Full orchestration (S3); provider abstraction (S2); parity test job (S4); unit/integration tests beyond the minimal skeleton smoke (S5).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, `python3 -m dso_ci_review.runner` invoked from a thin shim against a fixture diff produces a minimal valid `reviewer-findings.json` for one Anthropic specialist call via LiteLLM.
  ← Satisfies: "New `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/` Python package replaces bash orchestration"
- When this story is complete, the LiteLLM transport for both the Anthropic and OpenAI provider paths has been instantiated in the same configuration `providers/` will use, and the detected transport has been documented (httpx confirmed for both, OR pytest-httpx substituted for `respx` if `aiohttp` was detected on any path — do not rely on `DISABLE_AIOHTTP_TRANSPORT` or `httpx_client` per LiteLLM #12581/#13049).
  ← Satisfies: "Per-module unit tests using respx / httpx.MockTransport ... Story 1 transport-verification acceptance criterion"
- When this story is complete, the pre-migration golden corpus is captured as a checked-in deterministic baseline: input fixture diffs paired with LLM provider request/response artifacts (VCR cassettes or saved raw JSON) so re-running the parity test against the corpus produces identical findings every time.
  ← Satisfies: "Schema-equivalent reviewer-findings.json parity ... Pre-migration baseline captured as a checked-in golden corpus in story 1"
- When this story is complete, p50 and p95 pre-migration CI review-job duration on the fixture corpus is measured against the existing bash runner and recorded in a checked-in baseline file (paired later with S5's post-migration measurement to compute the delta).
  ← Satisfies: "CI run duration neutral-or-better ... compared to bash baseline captured before migration begins"

## Considerations

- [Testing] LiteLLM Router transport (httpx vs aiohttp) is ambiguous per LiteLLM #12581 — verify before any provider unit tests are written; do not rely on `DISABLE_AIOHTTP_TRANSPORT` or `httpx_client` (both have open reliability bugs).
- [Reliability] Epic is blocked by 5d6e-86a9 (CI parity port). Verify 5d6e-86a9 has merged AND its CI parity baseline is the one used for golden corpus capture — capturing pre-parity-port output produces a stale baseline that S4 will measure against incorrectly.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
